links.note: Was 30946 (most Bahais in India today are Indians), which has nothing to do with the item: why the Siddi community is designated a scheduled tribe. This chapter's 21 concepts include no Siddi concept and nothing on scheduled-tribe status. Cleared.

Was 30942 (Arab merchants who traded and stayed). The item asks who became Tibet's spiritual heads and rulers from the 15th century - Tibet-internal history, which no concept in this set covers. Cleared.

Was 30942 (traders who came to buy and settled), which inverts the item: the Siddis were brought to India as enslaved people BY traders. Neither 30932 nor 30947 fits either, since both are about people who sought refuge or opportunity - which is why I left the equivalent short answer unlinked. Cleared.

Was 30942 (Arab merchants). The copper plate is the Kerala Raja's grant to Jewish settlers, which answers 30932's question about what in Indian society let newcomers settle - where the other Kochi-grant items now sit.
Was 30950 (wherever Indians settle abroad), which is the opposite direction of travel. Where the Bene Israel settled in India belongs with the other flight-and-settlement items on 30932.
Was 30942 (Arab merchants). Who granted land to the Jews of Kerala is the reception question of 30932.
Was 30946 (the Indian Bahai community). The Siddis' cultural identity today is an integration question, which is 30932 - where the other Siddi integration items sit.
